exclusion_sets.note: TWO DISTINCT SETS, deliberately NOT merged into one 'excluded' flag, because they damage different axes.

shared_images.mechanism: warm multimodal encoder cache, keyed by image CONTENT
shared_images.axis_affected: TTFT ONLY; accuracy is unaffected, both models answered the same pixels

below_min_pixels.mechanism: image area below the 65,536 px min_pixels floor, so the DEVICE upscaled to the floor and the cloud (floor 4,096) did not
below_min_pixels.axis_affected: ACCURACY AND TTFT. The two models were shown DIFFERENT PIXELS, so a 2x2 cell on one of these reflects partly that the device got a larger rendering of the same photo. This is NOT only a token-count issue.

overlap.note: the fully clean subset is the paired set minus the UNION, not minus the sum of the two sizes unless they are disjoint.

shared_image_exclusion.rule: the repeated-image structure is a property of the DATASET itself, so it was present on both sides. The exclusion is therefore applied to BOTH columns or NEITHER: excluding from the cloud column alone would compare a cleaned column against an uncleaned one, an asymmetry introduced by the cleaning rather than by the data.
shared_image_exclusion.key: sha256 of the image as staged (PIL re-encode of the DECODED pixels), i.e. pixel content: the multimodal cache is keyed by processed image content, so byte-different but pixel-identical source images also hit (the source-byte key undercounted RefSpatial by 6)

register_after_counter_check.register: CENSUS: the observed per-dataset multimodal hit count equals the candidate count, so the exclusion set is exactly the set of warm-served questions, not an upper bound on it.

shared_image_exclusion.identifier_dedup_would_have_missed_this: the key is a sha256 of the DECODED pixels, not of the source bytes and not the identifier. The source-byte key undercounted RefSpatial by 6, and an identifier key cannot see this class at all: the multimodal cache is keyed by processed image content, so byte-different but pixel-identical images still hit it.

prompt_token_parity.verdict: IDENTICAL COUNTS on every question: identical visual input, CONFOUND CLEARED (subject to the vision-config dependency above)

ttft.denominator_note: TTFT uses its OWN denominator when the shared-image set is supplied: those questions are a warm-cache timing artifact and must leave the TTFT column, but they do NOT contaminate accuracy and are kept in it.

clean_denominators.rule: TWO DENOMINATORS, NOT ONE. Accuracy excludes the below-floor set ONLY, because the shared-image repeats are a TTFT-only artifact and dropping them from accuracy would discard questions for no reason. TTFT excludes BOTH, because the warm-cache repeats do contaminate timing. A single 'excluded' figure would either lose questions from accuracy or keep contaminated ones in TTFT.
